title: か (question)
meaning: Turns a statement into a question; also "or" between nouns.
simpleExplanation: か at the end of a sentence turns it into a question, like a spoken question mark: 学生です "is a student" → 学生ですか "Is (he) a student?". The word order does not change at all. Between two nouns, か means "or": お茶かコーヒー "tea or coffee". After a question word, か makes "some-": 何か "something", 誰か "someone".
whenUsed: Every yes/no question and question-word question in polite speech. In listening tasks, か is your signal that a question was asked and an answer is coming.
formation: Noun + か + Noun  (バスか電車)
Question word + か  (何か something, 誰か someone, どこか somewhere)

steps.en: Are you a student? (just add か)

examples.reading: あなたは がくせいですか。
examples.note: Statement + か = question. Nothing else moves.

examples.ja: お茶かコーヒーを飲みますか。
examples.reading: おちゃか コーヒーを のみますか。
examples.en: Will you have tea or coffee?

examples.note: 誰か = someone; the sentence-final か makes it a question.

examples.ja: この電車は新宿へ行きますか。
examples.reading: この でんしゃは しんじゅくへ いきますか。
examples.en: Does this train go to Shinjuku?
examples.note: A yes/no question in the polite form.

examples.ja: 週末はどこかへ行きましたか。
examples.reading: しゅうまつは どこかへ いきましたか。
examples.en: Did you go somewhere at the weekend?
examples.note: どこか = somewhere. Particles follow it: どこかへ.

similarGrammar.difference: ね asks for agreement ("right?"); か asks for information.
何か = something; 何も + negative = nothing.
In casual speech の can replace か at the end: 行くの？

commonMistakes.why: Particles stay in questions. か is added at the end; nothing else is dropped.

commonMistakes.wrong: 田中さんですか？ (with rising だ) 田中さんだか。
commonMistakes.why: In polite speech か follows です／ます. だ + か is not used in normal speech.

commonMistakes.wrong: コーヒーとお茶、どちらを飲みますか。→ コーヒーやお茶を飲みますか。
commonMistakes.right: コーヒーかお茶を飲みますか。
commonMistakes.why: "Or" between nouns is か. や means "and, among others".

usageNotes: Word order does not change for questions. A question mark is optional in Japanese writing. Question word + か = "some-" (何か something, 誰か someone, どこか somewhere).
jlptTips: If the sentence ends with a blank after ます or です and the options include か, ね, よ: a reply that starts with はい／いいえ means the blank is か.
何か / 誰か / どこか with an affirmative verb = some-; the same words with も and a negative verb = no-. Check the verb ending before answering.
